title: A digit utility module
brief: Create digits.h and digits.c with a declared/defined digitSum(int n) function. The main file should call it and print the sum of decimal digits.
input: One nonnegative integer N from 0 to 99999.
hints: Put function prototype in a guarded digits.h.
Implement the function in digits.c.
Use %10 and /10 to process digits.

title: Two utilities, one header
brief: Keep digitSum and add digitCount(int n), returning the number of decimal digits (zero has one digit).
input: One nonnegative integer N from 0 to 99999.
hints: Add the digitCount prototype to digits.h.
Implement digitCount in digits.c using a do/while loop.
Call both functions from main.

title: Repeatable dice rolls
brief: Use generator state=(state*5+1)%97; each new state yields a roll state%6+1. Simulate N rolls and print their sum. Do not call rand().
hints: Update state before computing each roll.
Roll values must be from one to six.
Accumulate rolls across N iterations.

title: Dice frequency histogram
brief: Keep the roll sum and report how many times each face 1 through 6 appeared, in order.
output: sum=S, then faces: A B C D E F with frequencies for faces 1–6.
hints: Allocate six counters initialized to zero.
Increase faces[roll-1] for each roll.
The six frequencies must sum to N.

title: Count positive values from a file
brief: Read N integers, write each to values.txt, close and reopen the file, then count numbers strictly greater than zero.
hints: Write one integer per line to values.txt.
Close and reopen for reading.
Count positive values while fscanf succeeds.

title: Filter readings to a second file
brief: Keep values.txt. While reading it, copy positive numbers only into filtered.txt, then reopen filtered.txt to calculate their total sum.
output: positive=C sum=S, where S is the sum of strictly positive values.
hints: Reopen values.txt after writing it.
Write positive entries to a separate file, then close both.
Read filtered.txt back to compute its sum.

title: Recursive integer power
brief: Write power(base,exponent) using recursion and the base case exponent=0. Do not call pow() from math.h.
hints: Return 1 when exponent is zero.
Return base times power(base,exponent-1).
Each recursive call must reduce exponent.

title: Fast recursive power with call count
brief: Replace linear recursion with exponentiation by squaring. Count every invocation of fastPower, including exponent=0; return both power and call count via an int* parameter.
output: power=P calls=C, where one call occurs for exponent zero and each other call recurses on exponent/2 once.
hints: Use an int* to count function invocations.
Recurse just once on exponent/2.
Square the half result, then multiply by base if exponent is odd.

title: A small circular queue
brief: Use an array of capacity 5 and head/tail indexes to process E X (enqueue) and D (dequeue) commands. All commands are valid and fit capacity.
input: K (0–20), then K commands E followed by integer [-100,100], or D. No overflow/underflow.

tests.label: Case 4
tests.input: 7 E 1 E 2 E 3 D D E 4 E 5

hints: Track head, tail and current size.
After incrementing an index, take modulo 5.
Front is at array[head] when size > 0.

title: Queue overflow and underflow protection
brief: Use the same circular queue but accept arbitrary commands: ignore enqueues when full and dequeues when empty, and count rejections.
input: K (0–40), then K commands E with integer [-100,100], or D.
output: size=N front=V rejected=R; front=-1 if empty.

tests.label: Case 4
tests.input: 7 E 1 E 2 E 3 E 4 E 5 E 6 E 7

tests.label: Case 5
tests.input: 9 E 1 E 2 E 3 E 4 E 5 D D E 6 E 7

hints: Reject D on an empty queue.
Reject E when size is already five, but still consume its integer.
Maintain wrapped head/tail indexes.
